# Work items: a unit of work with PEOPLE attached — who asked for it, who is
# doing it, who checks it, and where it has got to.
#
# Distinct from a stage (something breeze RUNS) and from an hours task (where
# time WENT). Kept in breeze's own state rather than in the hours database,
# because hours' schema is a third-party contract breeze refuses to write outside
# of, and workflow state belongs where the identities, roles, notifications and
# audit log already live.
env BREEZE_DIR=$WORK/state

exec breeze register identity alice
cp stdout alice.token
exec breeze register identity bob

exec breeze create task 'wire the audit read path' --assign bob --review alice --as alice
stdout 'w1 created'
# Assigning someone is itself news to them; alice is creator AND reviewer AND the
# actor, so she is not told what she just did.
stdout 'notified: bob'

exec breeze list tasks
stdout 'w1'
stdout 'open'
stdout 'bob'

# A change reaches the people attached MINUS the one who made it.
exec breeze update task w1 --status doing --as bob
stdout 'w1 \[doing\]'
stdout 'notified: alice'

# A name that is not a registered identity is refused: an item that LOOKS owned
# and notifies nobody is worse than an unassigned one.
! exec breeze create task 'x' --assign nobdy --as alice
stderr 'not a registered identity'

# The status vocabulary is closed, or it becomes six spellings of "in progress"
# across four agents and no query works.
! exec breeze update task w1 --status wip --as alice
stderr 'open, doing, review, done, blocked'

# A change that changes nothing notifies nobody — a "changed" message for a
# non-change teaches people to ignore the channel.
exec breeze update task w1 --status doing --as alice
stdout 'notified: \(nobody'

# A blocked item says what it is waiting for, in the list rather than behind
# --json: a status nobody can act on is not a status.
exec breeze update task w1 --status blocked --blocked 'waiting on the nvme' --as bob
exec breeze list tasks
stdout 'blocked: waiting on the nvme'

# Filters, so a board of any size stays answerable.
exec breeze list tasks --status blocked
stdout 'w1'
exec breeze list tasks --status done
stdout 'no tasks'

# Unassigning is a real operation and must be distinguishable from not mentioning
# the field — which is why the update fields are pointers on the wire.
exec breeze update task w1 --assign '' --as alice --json
# omitempty: a cleared assignee is ABSENT from the JSON, which is the proof it was
# cleared rather than silently retained.
! stdout '"assignee"'

exec breeze stop
